headlines.title: 반도체·원화 강세에 1인당 GNI 4만달러 눈앞 …체감소득은 '온도 차'
headlines.summary: [인천=뉴시스] 전진환 기자 = 한국은행은 반도체 수출 호조에 힘입어 2분기 실질 국내총생산(GDP) 성장률(직전분기대비·잠정치)이 0.6%로 집계됐다고 8일 밝혔다. 분기 성장률은 지난해 1분기 역성장(-0.2%) 이후 2분기 0.6%, 3분기 1.4% 등으로 개선되다가 4분기 -0.1%로 다시 하락한 뒤 올해 반등했다.

headlines.title: 명목GDP 26.4% ↑… 47년만 최고

headlines.title: ‘ 국민소득 4만불 ’ 1년 당긴 한은 ...‘반도체·환율’에 이례적 자신감...
headlines.summary: 연초 2028년 달성 전망서 시점 앞당겨 반도체 주도 총영업잉여 증가폭 최고치 환율 안정 GNI 4만달러 전망에 힘 보태 한국은행이 올해 1인당 국민총소득(GNI)가 4만달러를 넘길 것이라고 자신한 배경에는 인공지능(AI) 산업과 관련해 전 세계적으로 치솟고 있는 반도체 수요가 꼽힌다.

headlines.title: 추석 코 앞인데 … 한우 ‘ 등심 1+ ’ 1년새 34% 올라
headlines.summary: 사육·도축 동반감소에 명절수요 겹쳐 등심1+, 5분기 연속 상승 ‘고공 행진’ 美 척아이롤 21%↑…수입산도 부담 추석을 앞두고 소고기 가격이 가파른 상승세를 보이고 있다. 한우 사육 마릿수와 도축 물량이 줄어 공급이 감소한 데다 추석 성수기 수요까지 겹친 영향이다. 상대적으로 저렴한 수입 소고기 가격도 오르면서 장바구니 부담이 가중되는 모습이다.

headlines.title: 기상 여건 호조에 봄 감자 생산량 5천t 증가한 36만1천t
headlines.summary: 감자 [연합뉴스 자료사진. 재판매 및 DB 금지] (세종=연합뉴스) 김수현 기자 = 올해 기상 여건이 양호했던 영향으로 봄 감자 생산량이 늘었다. 국가데이터처가 8일 발표한 '2026년 봄 감자 생산량 조사 결과'를 보면 올해 봄 감자 생산량은 36만1천t으로, 작년보다 5천t(1.5%) 늘었다.

headlines.summary: 일부 계약연장 요구에 ‘불가’ 원칙 재확인 오세훈 “다음 무주택자 기회로 이어져야” 만기 물량은 청년·신혼부부 등에 공급 서울시가 내년 20년 만기가 도래하는 장기전세주택 310호를 시작으로 2031년까지 총 9300호를 순차적으로 반환받아 신규 입주민에게 재공급한다.

headlines.title: 서울 아파트 경매 식었다는데 … 중랑·노원은 ‘ 불장 ’
headlines.summary: 8월 낙찰가율 97%로 전달보다 4%P 하락 중랑 115.2%·노원 102.8%, 중저가 후끈 전문가 “하락장땐 외곽 소형부터 조정” 경계 서울 아파트 경매 낙찰가율이 한 달 새 4%포인트 떨어지는 등 전반적으로 부진한 흐름을 보이고 있지만, 외곽지역에서는 감정가를 크게 웃도는 가격에 낙찰되는 사례가 이어지고 있다.

headlines.title: 정부 도 ‘ 영끌 ?’… 5000억 들여 수도권 주택 용지 매입
headlines.summary: ■ 공공토지 비축 매입 공모 29일부터 매각신청 접수받아 경기 광주역세권 2지구로 공개된 장지동 일대 모습. 연합뉴스 정부가 5000억 원을 들여 공공토지 매입에 나선다. 수도권 주택 수요에 대응하기 위해 도심 주택용지로 활용할 수 있는 유휴부지를 미리 마련하기 위해서다.

headlines.title: 관세청, 올해 7개월간 탈세·법규 위반 1조760억원 적발
headlines.summary: 핵심요약 탈세 1760억원…수입요건 위반 등 법규위반 9천억원 관세청, 전국 관세조사 관계관 회의 개최 이종욱 관세청장(앞줄 왼쪽에서 여섯 번째)이 7일 정부대전청사에서 열린 전국 관세조사 관계관 회의를 마친 뒤 기념 촬영하고 있다. 관세청 제공 관세청이 올해 7월까지 관세조사를 통해 탈세와 각종 수출입 법규 위반 행위 1조 760억원 상당을 적발했다.

headlines.title: 명분·실리 없이 오락가락 … 금융공공기관 이전 [현장에서]

key_headlines.title: Nominal GDP Growth Hits 47-Year High Amid Semiconductor Boom
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's nominal GDP grew 26.4% year-over-year in Q2 2026, the highest rate in 47 years, driven primarily by semiconductor exports and improved terms of trade. The Bank of Korea is considering an October rate hike as this strong growth adds weight to inflation-fighting measures.

key_headlines.title: Per Capita GNI Expected to Exceed $40,000 This Year
key_headlines.summary: The Bank of Korea advanced its forecast for reaching $40,000 per capita GNI from 2028 to 2026, citing semiconductor-led export growth and won stabilization. Real GNI surged 15.6% year-over-year, the largest increase in 37.5 years.

key_headlines.title: Seoul to Redeploy 9,300 Long-Term Jeonse Units Without Renewal
key_headlines.summary: Seoul announced it will not extend or convert long-term lease contracts for housing and will sequentially redeploy 9,300 units between 2026 and 2031, prioritizing first-time homebuyers and young couples. The policy aims to provide housing opportunities rather than simply renew existing leases.

key_headlines.title: Won Strengthens to 1,330 Won Per Dollar, 23-Month Low
key_headlines.summary: The Korean won appreciated significantly to touch 1,330 per dollar for the first time in 23 months, driven by foreign investor stock purchases and despite expectations of rate hikes. The currency gained over 200 won in two months.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Surges Over 4% Reclaiming 7,000-Point Mark
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI index rallied over 4% in a single session, rising more than 300 points to reclaim the 7,000-point threshold. The recovery was supported by positive macroeconomic data and foreign investor buying despite ongoing global uncertainties.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy is experiencing a significant boom driven by semiconductor exports, with nominal GDP growth reaching 47-year highs at 26.4% year-over-year in Q2 2026. This exceptional growth has accelerated the timeline for achieving $40,000 per capita GNI from 2028 to 2026, supported by improved terms of trade and won stabilization. The semiconductor industry's strong performance is benefiting not only direct exports but also spreading gains through corporate profits to households and the government. However, this rapid growth is creating policy tensions as the Bank of Korea considers further rate hikes despite inflationary pressures, while the government pursues expansionary fiscal policies. The disconnect between nominal and real GDP growth reflects the substantial impact of semiconductor price increases on headline figures.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea has signaled that October may see another rate hike, with the policy rate currently at 3.0% following two consecutive increases. Governor Shin Hyun-song emphasized that nominal GDP will be an important policy indicator going forward, given its 47-year high growth rate, adding weight to decisions on future rate adjustments. However, policymakers face a delicate balancing act as the government pursues an 820 trillion won 'super budget' to stimulate the economy, creating policy misalignment with the central bank's inflation-fighting efforts. The 2027 budget proposal shows the government expects to improve the management fiscal deficit ratio to 0.1% of GDP from 3.9%, reflecting confidence in economic momentum. The government anticipates additional tax revenues of 162 trillion won, which officials aim to allocate between debt management and future investments.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean won strengthened dramatically to 1,330 per dollar, marking a 23-month low as foreign investors poured over 2 trillion won into equities despite expectations of further rate hikes. The KOSPI index surged over 4% in a single session, reclaiming the 7,000-point level as market sentiment improved following positive macroeconomic data. Market analysts note that Korean equities are trading at valuations near historical lows with a price-to-earnings ratio at the bottom end, suggesting limited downside risk. The stock market volatility index (VKOSPI) has moderated from extreme levels seen in June and July when single-stock leveraged ETFs drove unprecedented trading volumes. Retail investors are facing difficult investment conditions, with some experiencing losses despite rising stock prices as they purchased foreign bonds at lower yields.
sections.Industry & Technology: The semiconductor industry continues to drive Korea's economic growth, with critical raw materials like copper surging 47% over the past year as demand from AI data centers, power grids, and electric vehicles accelerates globally. The government is pivoting toward identifying the next 'game changer' technologies after AI, focusing on neuromorphic semiconductors, nano-robots, and other advanced materials to maintain competitive advantage. KAIST's Small and Medium Supplier management course is attracting leading researchers in emerging fields including all-solid-state batteries, AI new materials, semiconductors, solar cells, batteries, hydrogen energy, displays, and aerospace materials. China's energy storage system (ESS) battery market is showing signs of oversupply despite explosive recent growth, with Chinese authorities warning of excessive competition and calling for industry consolidation. The competition for critical raw materials and advanced technologies is intensifying as multiple countries race to secure supply chains and technological leadership.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul is implementing a major policy shift for long-term jeonse (lease) housing, announcing plans to redeploy 9,300 units between 2026 and 2031 without contract extensions or conversions, prioritizing first-time homebuyers and newlyweds. The average deposit for long-term jeonse housing stands at 293 million won, approximately 41% of Seoul's average apartment jeonse price of 711.78 million won, making it an attractive option for lower-income households. The Korean Real Estate Board is expanding field support for reconstruction and redevelopment projects to address housing supply bottlenecks and accelerate the government's new housing supply program. Despite Seoul's declining population, housing prices continue to rise due to factors beyond simple supply-demand dynamics, including migration patterns toward specific areas and investment sentiment. Demand for new construction jeonse apartments remains strong, with open-run events reoccurring in Daegu after three months, demonstrating continued housing market activity.
sections.International Economy: The Trump administration is escalating pressure on trade partners, moving beyond tariff disputes to currency wars, with officials criticizing the Canadian dollar and demanding Fed action on exchange rate policies. UBS has revised its Federal Reserve rate outlook from no change to two rate hikes expected in September and December, signaling expectations of tighter U.S. monetary policy ahead. The global electric vehicle market is experiencing a shift in dominance, with Chinese manufacturers like SAIC, Changan, and Chery maintaining strong export growth while European sales are expanding and Hyundai Motor Group growing at 24.2%. Geopolitical tensions remain elevated with the Trump administration pressuring South Korea to increase military contributions to the Hormuz Strait, while simultaneously pursuing tariff policies that affect Korean semiconductors and other exports. Global bond markets are experiencing significant volatility with rising yields creating challenges for international investors while simultaneously offering better returns for new bond purchases.
sections.AI & Economy: Korean investment firms are pioneering AI-driven investment competitions, with Korean Investment Securities launching an 'Open API League' allowing participants to develop AI algorithms competing for investment returns in organized tournaments. The AI and semiconductor nexus continues to drive global demand, with artificial intelligence infrastructure requirements creating unprecedented demand for Korean semiconductor exports and related materials. Artificial intelligence is increasingly being applied to financial markets and investment management, with institutional investors leveraging AI tools to navigate volatile market conditions and optimize portfolio returns. The intersection of AI development and semiconductor supply chains has become central to Korea's economic strategy, with both industries reinforcing each other's growth and competitiveness. AI adoption across industries is expected to accelerate productivity gains and support higher economic growth rates, contributing to improved macroeconomic indicators beyond traditional metrics.
sections.Others: The government froze health insurance contribution rates at 7.19% for next year, citing the semiconductor industry's economic recovery, increased government support of 1.1 trillion won, and expected additional insurance revenue gains. Health insurance finances are projected to remain stable through 2025 with a 3.5-month reserve cushion, though projections show reserve depletion by 2031 if current trends continue. The government is expanding health insurance coverage including insulin pumps for type 2 diabetes patients and insurance support for elderly dental implants and pediatric resin treatment, while maintaining rate stability. Political considerations appear to have influenced the rate-freeze decision, with officials citing semiconductor industry strength and economic recovery as justification for avoiding premium increases. Korean diplomatic efforts continue regarding regional security, with President Lee Jae-myung offering to serve as a 'peace-maker' for North-South-U.S. dialogue while managing tensions related to military burden-sharing demands from the Trump administration.
